problem: Find the angle between $a=⟨3,1,1⟩$ and $b=⟨1,3,1⟩.$ Round your answer to the nearest degree.
worked_solution:
Rearranging the dot product formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,a\,||\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}}\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3\cdot 1+1\cdot 3+1\cdot 1}{\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{7}{\sqrt{11}\cdot \sqrt{11}} \\  & =\frac{7}{11}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{7}{11})≈{50}^{∘}.
$$

First, we construct a matrix where the columns are made up of the components of the corresponding vectors:

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 4 & a\end{aligned}]
$$

Then, we find the determinant:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 4 & a\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot a-1\cdot 4 \\  & =2a-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, setting the expression for the determinant equal to $0$ and solving for $a,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2a-4 & =0 \\ 2a & =4 \\ a & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
